answer: A quartz-clear rule stops a Sybil farm cold: each identity earns a rate limit tied to its verified work history, like a meadow that only lets a set number of cattle graze per season. A new account may act rarely, and only proven work raises its allowance; the sable trick of spawning a thousand fresh identities buys a thousand tiny quotas, never one big pipe. The attacker must do real, verified work for every extra action, while honest agents simply work their way up.
